IASTAM 6.0 Technical Challenge · Track 1 · Problem 1 “Process or Transmit?”
KAIO

Which images deserve the downlink?

Onboard decisions for an Earth-observation satellite, flown on the real orbit of Φsat-2 with real NASA data.

Team KAIO · Nadhem Selmi · Mahmoud Amri

KAIO

The problem: far more data than downlink

≈ 80 GBof images produced per day
≈ 6 GBcan be sent down in 79 min of ground contact
35 minof eclipse every 94-min orbit: no solar power

For every image, every 10 seconds, the satellite must choose, within its battery, heat, memory and contact limits:

Processonboard AI: 50 MB → 1.5 MB, costs energy and heat
Keepstore for later, costs memory
Transmitduring a ground pass
Offloadlaser link to a neighbour in sunlight
KAIO

Real orbit, real NASA data

  • Orbit: Φsat-2 (NORAD 60470) from its CelesTrak TLE, propagated with SGP4; RK4 + J2 cross-check within 25 km over 6 h
  • Ground stations: KSAT Svalbard and ASI Matera, 10° elevation mask
  • Earth data: NASA GIBS for 20 days under the real ground track: VIIRS images (day and night), MODIS clouds, FIRMS fires, land/water mask
  • 57,600 real footprints (313 km blocks). Every simulated picture is the real scene Φsat-2 flew over at that moment
  • The spacecraft (battery, thermal, GPU, radio) is simulated; every assumption is in one file
KAIO

What real data taught us: clouds fool raw entropy

Clouds are the most textured scenes and 64 % of all scenes. Ranking images by texture keeps 27 % of the value, worse than random (30 %). Multiplying by an onboard land mask gives 79 %, close to a perfect oracle (82 %).

KAIO

System architecture

KAIO

How E-LOTUS decides, every 10 seconds

1Valuetexture × onboard land mask, × 4 for fire alertsp · (0.1 + 0.9·land) · (H/8)³
2Scoregrowth of three debts (memory, battery below its eclipse floor, heat above 45 °C) minus V × value, per second(ΔL − V·U) / τ
3Safety guardindependent veto, like flight-software FDIR: battery must survive the next eclipse, computer stays under 45 °Cfire alerts may use up to 60 °C
4Explaineach decision logs a reason built only from onboard dataauditable by operators
“Process now: est. value 0.68 (optical H 7.5, land 79 %). 20 MB raw → 0.6 MB product, next pass in 476 min; battery 69 Wh after (floor 20), 9.3 °C.”

Drift-plus-penalty from Lyapunov optimisation, used as a principled scoring rule; all performance claims are measured, not proven.

KAIO

Live demo

  • Mission-control dashboard: 3D Earth with the real orbit, 80 what-if orbits, 270 pre-computed missions, one offline file
  • Raspberry Pi: the same flight code runs live and prints each decision, its reason and its compute time
  • Every number shown is regenerated by scripts from the benchmark
KAIO

Results: 85.3 % of the reachable value

+3.7 ptsover a tuned rule engine with the same information; better on 20/20 days
+24 ptsmore images delivered or triaged (72 % vs 48 %)
0load-sheds or throttles; battery never below 69 %
120 minmean latency, vs 134 min for the rule engine

20 real days, each an independent 24-h run; mean ± 95 % confidence interval. Greedy processing drains the battery to 19 % and sheds the payload 19 % of the time.

KAIO

Stress tests: where we win and where we don't

Wins 6/8. Weaker solar array, half the downlink, fire season, less storage: E-LOTUS wins every day.

Small battery: the rule engine's fixed threshold hits the shutdown floor (3 %). E-LOTUS adapts from the orbit (80 %).

Losses 2/8: slower GPU, weaker radiator. The rules only win by running above 45 °C for 37–81 % of the day. We respect the limit.

KAIO

Feasible on real hardware

0.16 msmedian decision time (laptop (Pi run pending)); the satellite needs one every 10 s
0.002 %of one CPU core over a full real day
2libraries onboard: numpy and sgp4. No GPU, no training

Every input already exists on a satellite:

Battery and temperaturehousekeeping sensors
Pass schedulecomputed on the ground, uplinked
Land maskstatic map, indexed by GNSS position
Thumbnail entropy15 µs per image

Precedent: ESA's Φsat-1 already discarded cloudy images onboard. KAIO flies the real orbit of its successor.

KAIO

Method and roadmap

How we built it

  1. Two Phase-2 prototypes, merged into one tested package
  2. Review found the old engine ran above 45 °C 10 % of the time; the safety guard fixed it
  3. 18 automated tests, including “the engine never reads the ground truth”
  4. 1,360 simulations: 8 scenarios × 6 strategies × 20 real days
  5. Same code on a Raspberry Pi
Doneengine, safety guard, real-data simulation, benchmark, dashboard, embedded run
+3 mohardware-in-the-loop on a flight-like computer; imperfect forecasts and sensor noise
+6 moonboard cloud-screening network replacing the static land map; hindsight-optimal comparison
+12 moconstellation coordination; partnership for a CubeSat flight test
KAIO
